outcomes.text: Name the factors of production: land, labour, capital and enterprise.
Explain added value and how a business can increase it.
Explain opportunity cost.
Distinguish primary, secondary and tertiary sectors.
Distinguish private and public sectors.
Describe the characteristics of successful entrepreneurs.
Explain the purpose and key elements of a business plan.
Explain why a business plan is important.
Explain why governments support business start-ups.
Describe how governments support start-ups through grants, advice, cheap loans and training.

subtopics.title: The methods and problems of measuring business size

outcomes.text: Describe ways of measuring business size: employees, value or volume of output, capital employed.
Explain problems when measuring business size.

subtopics.title: Why some businesses grow and others remain small

outcomes.text: Explain why owners may want their business to grow.
Explain internal growth by developing new products or markets.
Explain external growth by mergers and takeovers, including horizontal and vertical integration.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of growth methods.
Explain problems linked to growth.
Explain why some businesses stay small.

subtopics.title: Why some businesses succeed and others fail

outcomes.text: Explain reasons for business success or failure, such as management skills, finance, product, demand, the economy and competition.
Describe sole traders, partnerships, private limited companies and public limited companies.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of each type of organisation.
Recommend and justify a suitable type of organisation for a given situation.

subtopics.title: Franchises, joint ventures and social enterprises

outcomes.text: Describe franchises, joint ventures and social enterprises.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of franchises for franchisor and franchisee.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of joint ventures.
Describe business objectives such as survival, growth, profit and market share.
Explain the importance of business objectives.
Describe internal stakeholders: owners, managers and employees.
Describe external stakeholders: customers, suppliers, lenders, government and the local community.
Describe the objectives of different stakeholder groups.
Explain how stakeholder objectives may conflict.
Describe the stages of recruitment: job description, person specification and job advertisement.
Describe selection methods: CV, application form, references, tests, assessment centres and interviews.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of internal and external recruitment.
Recommend and justify who to employ in a given situation.

subtopics.title: Employment contracts and legal controls over employment issues

outcomes.text: Describe the main contents of an employment contract.
Explain the benefits of contracts for employers and employees.
Describe legal controls: unfair dismissal, discrimination, health and safety and minimum wage.
Explain the effects of legal controls on employers and employees.
Explain the importance of training to a business and to employees.
Describe induction, on-the-job and off-the-job training.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of the three types of training.
Describe the main functional areas: operations, marketing, finance and human resources.
Explain tall and flat hierarchies, chains of command and spans of control.
Interpret simple organisational charts.
Describe flexible working such as home working and flexible hours.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of part-time and full-time employees.
Describe planning, organising, coordinating, commanding and controlling.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of delegation.
Describe autocratic, democratic and laissez-faire leadership.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of each style.
Recommend and justify a leadership style for a given situation.

subtopics.title: Why reducing the size of the workforce may be necessary

outcomes.text: Explain downsizing.
Explain reasons for reducing the workforce, such as automation, lower demand and cost cutting.
Explain redundancy.
Recommend and justify who to make redundant in a given situation.
Explain what a trade union is.
Explain the benefits of union membership to employees.
Explain why communication matters to a business.
Describe methods of communication: meetings, email, texts, social media, calls, letters, posters and noticeboards.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of different communication methods.
Distinguish internal and external communication.
Recommend and justify a communication method for a given situation.
Give examples of communication barriers.
Explain the reasons for communication barriers.
Explain problems caused by communication barriers.
Explain how communication barriers can be reduced or removed.

subtopics.title: The importance of a well-motivated workforce

outcomes.text: Explain why people work.
Explain the benefits of a motivated workforce: productivity, lower absenteeism, lower turnover and acceptance of change.
Outline the motivation theories of Maslow, Taylor and Herzberg.
Describe financial motivation methods: time rate, piece rate, salary, bonus, commission, profit sharing and fringe benefits.
Describe non-financial methods: job enrichment, job rotation, training, promotion, praise and employee of the month.
Recommend and justify a motivation method for a given situation.
Explain how marketing identifies customer needs.
Explain how marketing satisfies customer needs.
Explain how marketing maintains customer loyalty.
Explain how marketing builds customer relationships.
Explain how marketing anticipates changes in customer needs.
Explain why consumer spending patterns may change.
Explain why some markets are becoming more competitive.
Explain how businesses respond to changing spending and more competition.
Calculate market share.
Describe mass markets and niche markets.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of each.
Explain how markets can be segmented by age, income, location, gender and lifestyle.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of market segmentation.
Explain why businesses use market research.
Describe primary research: questionnaires, interviews, focus groups and observation.
Explain sampling and why it is useful.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of primary research.
Describe secondary research: competitor websites, government sources, reports and trade magazines.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of secondary research.
Explain factors affecting the accuracy of market research data.
Analyse simple market research data.
Explain the importance of brand image and the role of packaging.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of developing new products.
Describe the stages of the product life cycle.
Interpret a product life cycle diagram.
Describe extension strategies: new markets, new uses, adapting the product or packaging, and more advertising or promotion.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of extension strategies.
Recommend and justify an extension strategy for a given situation.
Describe pricing methods: cost-plus, competitive, penetration, skimming and dynamic.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of each pricing method.
Recommend and justify a pricing method for a given situation.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of distribution channels: direct, retailers, wholesalers and agents.
Recommend and justify a distribution channel for a given situation.
Explain reasons for promotion.
Describe sales promotion methods: vouchers, reward schemes, competitions and discounts.
Describe advertising methods: social media, targeted emails, leaflets and billboards.
Recommend and justify a sales promotion method for a given situation.
Recommend and justify an advertising method for a given situation.
Give examples of ecommerce: online banking, shopping and ticketing.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of ecommerce for businesses.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of ecommerce for customers.
Explain the importance of each element of the marketing mix.
Recommend and justify a marketing mix for a given situation.

subtopics.title: Entering new markets in other countries as a method of growth

outcomes.text: Explain advantages of entering overseas markets, such as more sales and spreading risk.
Explain disadvantages, such as cultural differences, lack of knowledge and legal requirements.
Explain the purpose of legal controls protecting customers from misleading promotion and faulty goods.
Explain the effects of these legal controls on marketing.
Calculate labour productivity.
Explain why efficiency is important to a business.
Explain how to increase efficiency through automation, technology and skills.
Explain lean production, just-in-time inventory control and Kaizen.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of lean production.
Explain why businesses hold inventory.
Explain the factors affecting how much inventory is held.
Describe job, batch and flow production.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of each method.
Recommend and justify a production method for a given situation.

topics.title: 4.2 Technology and production of goods and services

subtopics.title: The use of technology in the production of goods and services

outcomes.text: Explain how automation and mechanisation, such as CAM and 3D printing, change production.
Explain how technology improves productivity in services, such as contactless payments.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of technological change for businesses and employees.

topics.title: 4.3 Sustainable production of goods and services

subtopics.title: Methods of sustainable production of goods and services

outcomes.text: Explain how businesses can be more sustainable: renewable energy, less waste, reusing, recycling, eco-friendly products and packaging.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of becoming more sustainable.

topics.title: 4.4 Costs, scale of production and break-even analysis

outcomes.text: Classify and calculate fixed, variable, average and total costs.
Use cost data for simple decisions: which product, whether to stop production, what price, which supplier.
Explain economies of scale: purchasing, marketing, financial, managerial and technical.
Explain diseconomies of scale: poor communication, low loyalty, weak coordination and lack of control.
Explain break-even.
Complete or amend a simple break-even chart.
Interpret a break-even chart.
Calculate break-even output.
Define, calculate and interpret the margin of safety.
Use break-even analysis to judge changes in price, fixed costs and variable cost per unit.
Explain the limitations of break-even analysis.

subtopics.title: Why quality is important and how quality may be achieved

outcomes.text: Explain what quality means and why it matters.
Explain quality control.
Explain quality assurance.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of quality control and quality assurance.
Recommend and justify quality control or assurance for a given situation.

subtopics.title: Main factors which influence location decisions

outcomes.text: Explain factors influencing the location of a manufacturing business.
Explain factors influencing the location of a service business.
Explain factors in choosing which country to locate operations in.
Recommend and justify a location for a given situation.
Explain why businesses need finance: start-up, expansion, replacing assets, new technology and working capital.
Distinguish short-term and long-term finance needs.
Explain working capital and why it matters.
Describe internal sources: owners' investment, retained profit, sale of assets and working capital.
Describe external sources: shares, venture capital, overdrafts, leasing, hire purchase, loans, trade credit, grants and crowdfunding.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of internal and external sources.
Explain factors in choosing a source of finance.
Recommend and justify a source of finance for a given situation.

subtopics.title: The importance of cash and cash flow forecasts

outcomes.text: Explain why cash matters to a business.
Explain what a cash flow forecast is and why it matters.
Describe its features: inflow, outflow, net cash flow, opening and closing balance.
Amend or complete a simple cash flow forecast.
Interpret a simple cash flow forecast.
Explain ways to overcome a short-term cash flow problem.

subtopics.title: What is profit and why it is important

outcomes.text: Explain what profit is.
Explain why profit matters to private sector businesses.
Describe the features: revenue, cost of sales, gross profit, expenses and profit.
Make simple calculations from a statement of profit or loss.
Make decisions based on simple statements of profit or loss.

subtopics.title: The main elements of a statement of financial position

outcomes.text: Describe non-current assets and current assets.
Describe non-current liabilities and current liabilities.
Explain capital employed.
Calculate total assets, total liabilities and working capital.
Make decisions based on simple statements of financial position.
Explain profitability.
Calculate and interpret gross profit margin, profit margin and ROCE.
Explain liquidity.
Calculate and interpret the current ratio and acid test ratio.
Describe internal users of accounts and ratio analysis.
Describe external users of accounts and ratio analysis.
Explain how users use financial information to make decisions.
Explain the limitations of accounts and ratio analysis.
Describe the stages of the business cycle: growth, boom, recession and slump.
Explain how each stage may affect a business.
Explain the effects of changes in employment, inflation and economic growth.
Explain the effects of tax changes on business profit.
Explain the effects of tax changes on people's income.
Explain the effects of changes in government spending.
Explain the effects of changes in interest rates.
Explain how businesses respond to changes in taxes and interest rates.
Explain reasons for globalisation: transport, technology, free trade agreements and newly industrialised countries.
Explain opportunities and threats of globalisation.
Describe import tariffs and quotas.
Explain their effects on businesses.
Explain the advantages to a business of becoming an MNC.
Explain advantages to a host country, such as jobs, exports, choice and investment.
Explain disadvantages to a host country, such as competition, environmental damage, resource use and repatriated profits.
Explain external costs and benefits of business decisions.
Explain appreciation and depreciation of an exchange rate.
Explain how exchange rate changes affect importers and exporters.
Explain how business activity harms the environment.
Explain why businesses respond to environmental issues.
Explain how businesses respond to environmental issues.
Explain the effects of environmental legal controls on how, what and where to produce or sell and on costs.
Describe ethical issues such as child labour, fair wages, fair prices and environmentally responsible suppliers.
Explain how businesses may respond to ethical issues.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of being ethical.
Explain how pressure groups influence business decisions.
